Subject: ACME MSA + Order Form — marketing & confidentiality redlines

Hi Emma —

Thanks again for the helpful conversation today. Per our call, I’m attaching the current MSA + Order Form (v3) with the marketing/publicity and confidentiality sections highlighted. We want to keep things simple for both sides but understand ACME’s sensitivity around press and logo usage.

Two specific asks from ACME I wanted to capture here so we can iterate quickly:
- Can we remove the unilateral press/announcement language and replace with a mutual-approval requirement?
- Logo/reference rights: ACME prefers only a short customer list on our site rather than a public case study or press release without prior sign-off.

If you can send back a marked-up redline or call out exact language you want removed/added, I’ll loop in Legal (cc’d: Dev, Laura) and get a final position from our side today. We’re targeting a signed order this week, so if we can resolve the publicity clause it will unblock procurement.

Attachments: ACME_OrderForm_redlines.pdf, Redwood_MSA_v3_redline.docx

Thanks —
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jersey-style signature
From: Emma Hartman <emma@acmecloud.com>

Date: Mon, 09 Feb 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ACME MSA + Order Form — marketing & confidentiality redlines

Jordan —

Appreciate the doc. We did a quick internal review and would like to propose the following redlines on publicity/reference:
1) Strike the current "we may issue press releases" clause.
2) Replace with: "Neither party will issue a press release referencing the other party's name, logo, or specific results without the other party's prior written consent."
3) Logo listing is acceptable for a "customer" page limited to a logo strip with no case study or performance metrics; customer logo use by Redwood must be limited to ACME's publicly available logo art.
4) Any customer-specific case study or joint press announcement requires a separate SOW and mutual sign-off.

We’ve attached a single pdf with our redlines. Also, because this involves marketing exposure, LegalOps wants confirmation of where logos will be displayed (site, sales deck, etc.) and a promise that we won’t use quotes or metrics without explicit approval.

If you can confirm Redwood’s stance on the bullets above, we can move forward.

Best,
Emma
Director, Strategic Partnerships | ACME Cloud

Dev/Laura —

Looping you both in for legal redline guidance. ACME wants to remove our current announcement language and limit logo/reference rights. Key asks from them above. Can we propose a compromise that preserves Redwood’s customer reference needs while addressing ACME’s marketing sensitivity?

Two priorities: (1) get wording that Legal is comfortable with so procurement can sign this week; (2) avoid a permanent ban on case studies — maybe a staged permission (e.g., allow logo + customer list, case study only after 6 months and with approval).

FWIW, deal is standard ARR, low-risk, would like to keep this simple.

-Jordan
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.inference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: ACME MSA + Order Form — marketing & confidentiality redlines

Jordan —

Thanks for the context. Suggested positions below that should be acceptable to ACME while preserving Redwood’s ability to reference the customer for sales/marketing purposes. I recommend we send this as a short replacement clause rather than negotiating inline edits.

Proposed publicity/reference clause (redline suggestion):
- "Press Announcements and Publicity: Neither party shall issue any press release or public announcement referencing the other party or the existence of a commercial relationship without the other party's prior written consent, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld or delayed. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Redwood may list ACME Cloud on a customer/reference page on its public website and in sales materials, limited to ACME's company name and logo, provided such use is consistent with ACME's published brand guidelines and does not include confidential performance metrics or customer quotes. Any case study or co-branded press announcement will require separate written approval and will be governed by a mutually agreed statement of work."

Confidentiality carve: add explicit callout that marketing materials cannot contain Confidential Information as defined in the MSA and that "Confidential Information" exclusions apply (e.g., information publicly known or independently developed).

Other notes:
- Recommend a 30-day review window for marketing approvals in the clause to keep sign-off timelines bounded.
- If ACME insists on removing all logo use, consider offering a narrow exception: listing in a non-prominent "customers" roster only.

I attached a one-page redline for your review (Redwood_MSA_v3_redline.docx). If you want, I can prepare the exact language for Jordan to send to Emma.

-Dev
Legal Counsel | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: ACME MSA + Order Form — marketing & confidentiality redlines

Emma —

Thanks for the clear feedback and the redline. Per our internal legal review, we can accept the mutual-consent approach with the following clarifications:

- We will replace the unilateral press-release language with Dev's proposed clause (copy below).
- Redwood may list ACME on a customer/reference page (logo + company name) provided we follow ACME brand guidelines and do not publish quotes or metrics without prior approval.
- For case studies/co-branded press, we require a separate SOW and mutual sign-off; Redwood proposes a 30-day approval timeline for marketing materials.

Proposed inserted text (excerpt):
"Press Announcements and Publicity: Neither party shall issue any press release or public announcement referencing the other party or the existence of a commercial relationship without the other party's prior written consent, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld or delayed. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Redwood may list ACME Cloud on a customer/reference page on its public website and in sales materials, limited to ACME's company name and logo, provided such use is consistent with ACME's published brand guidelines and does not include confidential performance metrics or customer quotes. Any case study or co-branded press announcement will require separate written approval and will be governed by a mutually agreed statement of work. Marketing approvals will be provided within thirty (30) calendar days of submission or deemed approved."

I’ve uploaded the redlined MSA/Order Form and created a DocuSign envelope for the Order Form to keep momentum: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3cACME-redlines and https://www.docusign.com/ACME-MSA-4932.

If that language looks good to you, I can get the order out today.

Thanks —
